unit.why: One frame narrative: R. Berish of Oshpitsin foretells that his follower's sick, childless wife will be helped by a rebbe who will come to Vishnitsa, and the prediction comes true. Inside it he tells a story about a hasid in Kshanov and a homily on Abraham and Isaac.

stories.start_quote: איש אחד ממקורבי הה״ק ר׳ בעריש נחלה
stories.end_quote: נסעו אליו אנשים רבים בפרסום גדול
stories.summary_en: R. Berish of Oshpitsin, after telling tales of tsaddikim, repeatedly predicts that his follower Menahem ben Gitel will find salvation through a rebbe yet to come to Vishnitsa. In an embedded tale he defends the R. of Sinyawa's humility against a proud hasid. When the rebbe arrives, four Oshpitsin men travel to him secretly; he receives them warmly by ruah ha-kodesh and blesses the man, giving him an herb. The wife recovers and conceives, despite opposition in the town, and many then travel to the rebbe.
